review_notes: I reviewed the whole file (lines 1–30), which contains two theorems. In `uniform_index_of_increasing_open_cover`, I checked the signature of `IsCompact.elim_directed_cover` and found the Mathlib lemma `Monotone.directed_le`. Mathlib's `CompactExhaustion.exists_superset_of_isCompact` (SigmaCompact.lean line 382) passes `Monotone.directed_le` as the `Directed (· ⊆ ·)` argument of `elim_directed_cover`. That makes the replacement very likely to work here, but I have not compiled it. I also looked at `uniform_strict_index`. It uses `lt_iSup_iff` from Mathlib/Order/CompleteLattice/Defs.lean, which is the right lemma. Its other steps are already short. Changing `lt_of_lt_of_le` to dot notation would be a matter of taste, so I did not report it. I also left the `obtain`/`exact` split in the first proof alone: folding it into `.imp` would be shorter but not easier to read.

findings.excerpt:
(fun τ _ => Set.mem_iUnion.mpr (hcover τ)) (by
      intro i j
      exact ⟨max i j, hmono (le_max_left i j), hmono (le_max_right i j)⟩)
findings.problem: The proof needs the cover to be directed. It proves this by hand: it unfolds `Directed`, picks `max i j` as the common upper bound, and applies `hmono` to both `le_max` facts. Mathlib already has `Monotone.directed_le`, which says a monotone family on a directed order is directed. The inline block repeats that general fact.
findings.proposed_change:
Replace the `(by intro i j; exact ⟨max i j, …⟩)` argument with the lemma:

  obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := isCompact_univ.elim_directed_cover U hopen
    (fun τ _ => Set.mem_iUnion.mpr (hcover τ)) hmono.directed_le
  exact ⟨k, fun τ => hk (Set.mem_univ τ)⟩
findings.benefit: This removes a three-line tactic block. The reader sees the actual reason the cover is directed: "U is monotone, so it is directed." They no longer have to check a `max` witness. Mathlib uses the same idiom for the same hypothesis of `elim_directed_cover`. The proof still visibly follows its plan: a compact space, an open directed cover, and one index that covers everything.
